The task is complete. Summary of the repair:

## What was wrong in the starter
- `/65`–`/128` prefixes were **silently skipped** instead of rejected
- **No duplicate detection** for normalized prefixes
- **Prefix boundaries were confused with winning routes** — it emitted one row per prefix rather than the winning interval function
- **Partial batches were dropped** (`i+batch<=size`), small tables lost their default row, and `std::stoul` accepted signs/whitespace in batch sizes
- **No image validation whatsoever**; trace lines weren't whitespace-trimmed

## The new implementation (`/work/submit/planb64.cpp`, 553 lines)
- **`build`**: strict FIB parsing (`inet_pton(AF_INET6)` validation, lengths 0–64 with leading zeros allowed, 32-bit hops, duplicate normalized networks rejected), then an **O(n log n) stack sweep** over candidate change points (key 0 plus every prefix start and end below 2⁶⁴). Since prefix ranges are dyadic they form a laminar family, so covering prefixes at any key form a chain ordered by length — the stack top is always the winner. Rows are emitted only where the `(hop, length)` pair actually changes, yielding exactly the minimal canonical serialization, independent of FIB order.
- **`lookup`**: full canonical image validation (header/version, count match, 16 lowercase hex digits, unpadded decimals, strict ordering, first key zero, pair ranges, one-sided no-match, equal adjacent pairs, final newline, extra records, spacing), full trace validation, then predecessor (binary) search per query. Scalar and batch are semantically identical; output is buffered so nothing is printed before complete validation.
- **Errors**: exit 2, empty stdout, `ERROR:`-prefixed stderr; failed builds stage through a temp file + rename so the destination is never disturbed.

## Verification performed
- Public check: byte-identical image and all three lookup outputs
- 344 randomized/structured cross-checks against an independent brute-force reference; boundary consistency at every image row; at-scale checks (200 000-record FIBs, 400 001-row images, 1 000 000-record traces) against an independent mask-the-query LPM
- 177 error/edge cases (arguments, FIB, trace, image mutations) — all exit 2 with empty stdout
- UBSan and libstdc++ debug-mode runs of every suite (ASan cannot run in this sandbox: it requires `/proc/self/maps`)
- Fresh-tree builds under many external `CXX`/`CXXFLAGS` combinations, command-line and environment overrides, parallel make
- Worst case: build 0.09 s, 1 M lookups against a 400 001-row image 0.35 s, memory under 64 MiB

Three real bugs were caught by the test suites during development (a narrowing cast that corrupted hop 4294967295 into `-1`, an `argc==1` segfault, and a line-length check that fired on whole read chunks).
